newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: E.Asia Oilseeds - Japanese, Korean buyers sidelined.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds - Japanese, Korean buyers sidelined.

text.p: South Korean and Japanese oilseed importers are seen keeping a low profile during the seasonally slow summer holiday period, dealers said on Monday.
Some buyers in the two countries may buy prompt oilseed shipments if futures prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) fall from their current levels, they said.
"We don't expect any big business in the summer holidays unless prices fall much further," a trader in Korea said.
He said Korean buyers normally hold back on buying during the summer vacation period, which lastd from the end of July until mid-August.
In Japan, traders said they would continue to wait for lower-priced new crop U.S. soybeans which will become available from October.
"The situation is almost unchanged since last week," a soybean trader at a major trade house in Japan said. "We're waiting for further price drops."
Some traders said they are awaiting figures for local soybean crushing and soy product output for June, which will be released by Japan's Agriculture Ministry on Tuesday.
The country's soybean crushing in May totalled 318,628 tonnes, up 7.8 percent from a year earlier, and soyoil and soymeal output were 57,089 and 242,116 tonnes, respectively.
